task:
Repair the completed issue #537 implementation on exact source branch `codex/run-33434623997-1` at commit `6fb1349d750d9f64933b7885de4533a834ded285` before it is proposed for merge. Start from current origin/main at `fd64ef8e14b5b026cec2d14949115ab681fb0b7d`. Read CLAUDE.md, docs/ROADMAP.md, the issue #537 implementation diff, all seven changed files, and all focused tests. Fetch the exact source commit and reproduce its seven-file change in this isolated working tree using it as source material; do not modify the source branch. Preserve its two-pass/no-output-before-preflight design, schema-v2 manifest/receipt, deterministic archive, JSON structural redaction, path/symlink/size guards, no-stale workflow staging/publish handoff, documentation, and read-only/no-DB/no-host-mutation boundary. The wrapper will commit and push; do not commit, push, merge, deploy, access a remote host, download or inspect artifact 9773572090, reveal or guess any real credential, rotate credentials, delete artifacts, touch production, modify databases, change DNS, start/stop containers, implement #527, or alter Stage 27/product/data/CRE/CPE/Journal behavior. Use synthetic fixtures only.

Independent review found the following precision and coverage defects. Treat them as valid unless concrete code/test evidence disproves one; report any disproven item explicitly.

1. Ordinary text assignment scanning is too broad. The case-insensitive assignment regex can treat Python annotations (`API_TOKEN: str`), comparisons (`TOKEN == other`), and dynamic expressions (`TOKEN = get_token()`) as literal secrets and replace valid source code. Narrow transformations to high-confidence literal assignments. An assignment operator must not consume `==`, `:=`, or type annotations. For Python and other source files, redact only quoted literal secret values and credential-bearing URI literals, not unquoted expressions or identifiers. Shell/YAML/env-style text may redact a clearly literal unquoted assignment where appropriate. Support Dockerfile/Containerfile `ENV` and `ARG` sensitive assignments. Do not break comments, prose, identifiers, annotations, comparisons, or function calls. Add focused tests proving these remain verbatim while quoted literal assignments and Dockerfile `ENV POSTGRES_PASSWORD=synthetic-secret` are safely redacted.

2. Reject binary-like text before archive emission. At minimum, any selected payload containing NUL (`\x00`) must fail preflight with a value-free error and produce zero output bytes. Preserve invalid-UTF-8 fail-closed behavior and add a no-output regression test. Consider rejecting other disallowed control bytes only where deterministic and non-disruptive.

3. Expand safe template/sentinel recognition to common CHANGEME-style forms used in this repository, especially `REPLACE_ME`, `REPLACE-ME`, and prefixed forms such as `REPLACE_ME_WITH_...`, without treating arbitrary natural-language values as templates. Add tests proving these remain verbatim.

4. A credentialed URI is safe when its password component is an explicit template/sentinel even if the username is literal. For example `postgresql://app:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}@db/example` must remain verbatim. Align the sanitizer and final unsafe scan so this form is not first accepted then rejected, or needlessly redacted. Add PostgreSQL and Redis template tests as applicable.

5. Recognise AWS temporary access-key IDs as well as long-lived IDs: cover both `AKIA[A-Z0-9]{16}` and `ASIA[A-Z0-9]{16}` using synthetic values, with the existing exclusion/fail-closed contract and no matched value in errors/metadata.

6. Cover high-confidence credential query parameters in PostgreSQL/Redis URLs, such as a literal `password=` query value, without corrupting unrelated query parameters. Explicit template values in those parameters remain verbatim. Add focused redaction and template tests.

7. Keep the validation scan genuinely independent of the production scanner: construct a synthetic archive and inspect every member with separately declared high-confidence patterns for private-key headers, GitHub/OpenAI/AWS key formats, credentialed PostgreSQL/Redis authority components, sensitive literal assignments, and literal password query parameters. Do not simply call the production `_unsafe` function and describe that as independent.

8. Add a consistency regression proving every would-be archive payload passes both the production final re-scan and the independent scan, while manifest and receipt contain no matched value. Preserve deterministic bytes and original/sanitized hashes/dispositions.

Use only the existing pinned `tests/requirements-ci.txt` if test tools are missing. Run the complete recovery/operator/workflow-focused suite, tests/test_ci_stall_detection.py, relevant repo-hygiene tests, Ruff check and format on changed Python, parse changed workflow YAML with pinned PyYAML, independent synthetic archive scan, and `git diff --check`. End with exact files, exact results, the source commit reproduced, each finding's disposition, and limitations: artifact deletion, credential active-use/rotation, and a real recovery rerun were not performed.
